clue.text: Australian in old South African pub

indicators.note: the Australian piece is placed inside the South African one

parts.note: a Boer was a Dutch-descended settler of old South Africa
Oz is slang for Australia or an Australian

explanation.surface: An Aussie drinking in a bar run by an elderly South African.
explanation.walkthrough: A BOOZER is British slang for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal British synonym: a drinking establishment or bar is called a boozer.

parts.note: a BA is a Bachelor of Arts, a graduate

indicators.note: off means awry or wrong, so these letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A graduate wipes chalk marks off, perhaps as a criticism.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges CHALKS into CKLASH.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile reaction: a strong public reaction against something is often a flood of critical remarks.

parts.note: once can mean as soon as, or when
something done or finished is over

explanation.surface: A brief inspection carried out once it is finished.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a quick inspection or glance is called this.

indicators.note: the goddess goes about, around, the right

parts.note: Eos is the Greek goddess of the dawn

explanation.surface: A goddess swapped for a god, roughly correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Greek deity of love is a god.

clue.text: Important people covering items of underwear with jumpers

indicators.note: the jumpers go over and around the underwear, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: tops are upper garments such as jumpers (British for sweaters)
bras are items of women's underwear

explanation.surface: Dignitaries wearing sweaters over their lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: A jumper is the British word for a sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the senior officers or bosses of an organisation are its top brass.

definitions.meaning: a wild clematis with fluffy seed heads
facial hair on a father, the old man in slang

explanation.surface: A plant growing on one's father.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old man' is British slang for father, so his whiskers fit the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Plant name: the clematis Clematis vitalba is known by this popular name.

definitions.meaning: a prison sentence, in British slang

explanation.surface: A variant of 'time flies'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doing bird' is British slang for serving prison time.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: rhyming slang (birdlime) for a jail term, and a feathered creature.

clue.text: Ridiculous putting a bendy bus on road

indicators.note: something bendy is bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted

explanation.surface: Putting an articulated bus on the road is silly.
explanation.walkthrough: A bendy bus is a British name for an articulated bus.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something ludicrous or preposterous is absurd.

indicators.note: the always piece sits inside, blocking the pipe

parts.note: to pipe up is to sing out
ay is an old poetic word for always

explanation.surface: A garden gnome always stuck in a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gnome' looks like a garden ornament; it is also a pithy maxim.
explanation.definitionFit: Rare sense: a gnome is a short maxim or aphorism, an old proverb.

definitions.meaning: crazy or silly, an informal adjective
the European bird famous for its call and for laying eggs in other nests

explanation.surface: A foolish bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: informal adjective meaning mad, and the name of a well-known bird.

clue.text: A year after building raised, probably

indicators.note: the A and year come after the rearranged letters
building means putting together afresh, so the letters of raised are reassembled

explanation.surface: Something raised a year after construction began, probably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' looks like a noun for a structure, but it signals the letters being put together anew; 'after' places the A and year at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Phrase equivalence: saying 'I dare say' signals that you think something is likely.

indicators.note: an unfortunate arrangement implies the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Family members who regrettably are not thin.
explanation.definitionFit: Family relations: a spouse's mothers are relatives by marriage.

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, as is loo

indicators.note: the first of the word marks only its opening letter being taken

explanation.surface: A Beatles reference: John and Paul, and perhaps a Ringo-style ring.
explanation.walkthrough: John and Paul look like Lennon and McCartney; John is a toilet, LOO, and Paul gives only P.
explanation.definitionFit: Shape synonym: a closed curve or circle of rope is both a ring and a loop.

indicators.note: a tooth operated on is worked over, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dentist works on the right-hand molar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right' looks like a direction; it is the noun-like adjective meaning ethical.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something ethically correct or virtuous is moral.

indicators.note: called back, so the missing words of the phrase are read in reverse

parts.note: the phrase 'neither you nor I' is left unfinished; the missing words are NOR I

explanation.surface: A broken-off remark: neither you... is recalled.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash invites completing 'neither you nor I'; the missing NOR I, recalled (reversed), gives the metal.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the metal Fe is a chemical element.

indicators.note: secretes means hides away, so the figure hides the line within

parts.note: four is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A figure hiding a line of white powder, like a drug smuggler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'secretes' looks like oozing; it means hides.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: ground wheat used in baking is a white powder.

indicators.note: the payment word takes the A inside it

parts.note: a cost is a payment or price

explanation.surface: A payment including a cash float.
explanation.walkthrough: 'float' looks like petty cash; it means move without effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to drift along freely without power is to glide or float along.

clue.text: Last two, he and she out to attract the most attention

indicators.note: out means wrong or disordered, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: The final pair, a man and a woman, come out to grab the spotlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges LASTTWOHESHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: a performer who outshines everyone else on stage is said to do this.

parts.note: bad means rotten or spoiled
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A rib becomes rotten in time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ribbing' looks anatomical; it means teasing.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: playful teasing or banter is ribbing.

clue.text: Dynamic forces around Open University, certainly

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the university
dynamic means energetic and changing, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the OU is Britain's distance-learning university

explanation.surface: Energetic forces surround the Open University, assuredly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dynamic' reads as describing the forces but is the signal to rearrange them; 'around' then wraps them about the university's initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: saying something is so without doubt is to say certainly.

clue.text: Pole once finding accommodation on river

indicators.note: in a down-or-across charade, on places the first piece before the second

parts.note: quarters are lodgings or living accommodation
the Taff is a river in Wales flowing through Cardiff

explanation.surface: A Polish person once found lodgings by a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality but means a stout stick.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical weapon: a long wooden staff once used for fighting in England.

parts.note: a jockey's mount is the horse ridden in a race

explanation.surface: A buyer asks the price of a racehorse.
explanation.definitionFit: Equivalence: asking how much asks for the quantity or sum.

clue.text: In France, I haul up part of ship that's been thrown overboard

parts.note: je is French for I

indicators.note: in a down clue, hauling up reads the word bottom to top

parts.note: the mast is part of a ship

explanation.surface: A sailor in France hauls part of a ship's gear overboard.
explanation.definitionFit: Maritime term: goods jettisoned from a ship to lighten it are jetsam.

indicators.note: judged by the ears, so the word is taken as it is heard

parts.note: meat is animal flesh used as food

explanation.surface: A question about feeling flesh near the ears.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: two lines or surfaces that touch are said to come together.

indicators.note: the black piece is put inside the word for sack

parts.note: to sack someone is to fire them
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Black thread found inside a sack.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a single filament or strand of material is a fibre.

clue.text: Writer in author I bossed around

indicators.note: turned around, so the found letters read backwards
the letters are found within the run of clue words

explanation.surface: A writer inside an author whom I ordered about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' finds ORIB in the clue words and 'around' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a ballpoint pen is a writing implement, and Biro is a British brand name for one.

definitions.meaning: a small quantity, as of salt

explanation.surface: Two words a cook might use.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a splash or small amount, and vigour or élan.

parts.note: in can mean at, as in a place
the altar stands for its building; CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A creep standing at the altar, perhaps marrying.
explanation.walkthrough: Being at the altar is being in church, IN CH.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to move very slowly forward is to creep.

clue.text: Rocky somewhere in Bedfordshire, initially lost

indicators.note: the first letter goes missing from the town

parts.note: Dunstable is a market town in Bedfordshire, an English county

explanation.surface: Rocky, a place in an English county, loses its first letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially lost' drops the D from DUNSTABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something wobbly or shaky is rocky.

clue.text: Not just a run, if jumping

indicators.note: jumping letters leap about into a new order

explanation.surface: A sprint becomes a jump, which seems not merely a run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'only'; here it means fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonym construction: a decision that lacks justice or fairness is unjust.

clue.text: Male, a belligerent killer on reservation?

parts.note: a tom is a male animal, especially a cat
a hawk is a person favouring war

explanation.surface: A warlike man commits a killing on a reservation.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the definition by example: a weapon of Native American peoples.
explanation.definitionFit: Weapon association: a light axe used by Native Americans, linked to life on a reservation.

definitions.meaning: a cunning scheme or ruse, informal British

explanation.surface: A clever stunt that leaves people gasping.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: British slang for a crafty scheme, and noisy laboured breathing.
